quests.instruction: Shadow the reply. Inside 'going', which sound bridges the vowels of 'go' and 'ing'?
quests.word: I was going to ask you the same thing.
quests.textToSpeak: I was going to ask you the same thing.
quests.ipa: /aɪ wəz ˈɡəʊɪŋ tʊ ˈɑːsk jʊ ðə ˈseɪm ˈθɪŋ/
quests.hint: Feel your lips round slightly after /əʊ/.
quests.explanation: After the rounded vowel /əʊ/, the lips move through a /w/ glide before /ɪ/.
quests.flowRule: Vowel-to-Vowel Glides: after rounded vowels such as /uː/ and /əʊ/, a /w/ glide fills the gap.

quests.instruction: Shadow the suggestion. What glide links 'may' and 'ask'?
quests.word: You may ask her tomorrow, if you like.
quests.textToSpeak: You may ask her tomorrow, if you like.
options: A /w/ glide fills the gap between the two vowels
A light /j/ slides between /eɪ/ and /ɑː/: may-yask
No glide at all: a hard stop separates 'may' and 'ask'
quests.correctAnswer: A light /j/ slides between /eɪ/ and /ɑː/: may-yask
quests.ipa: /jʊ ˈmeɪ‿ˈɑːsk hə təˈmɒrəʊ ɪf jə ˈlaɪk/
quests.hint: Say 'may' and notice where your tongue is as the vowel ends.
quests.explanation: 'May' ends in the high-front glide of /eɪ/ and 'ask' begins with a vowel, so a light /j/ bridges the two without a break.
quests.flowRule: Vowel-to-Vowel Glides: after /eɪ/, /aɪ/ and /iː/, a /j/ glide bridges to the next vowel.

quests.instruction: Shadow the plan. In 'try a', what bridges the /aɪ/ and the /ə/?
quests.word: I'd like to try a new Thai place on Friday.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd like to try a new Thai place on Friday.
options: A /w/ glide, because the lips round before the vowel
An /r/ glide, because the spelling has an r
quests.ipa: /aɪd ˈlaɪk tə ˈtraɪ‿ə ˈnjuː ˈtaɪ ˈpleɪs ɒn ˈfraɪdeɪ/
quests.hint: Listen to where your tongue sits at the end of 'try'.
quests.explanation: /aɪ/ finishes high at the front of the mouth, so a light /j/ appears before the weak vowel of 'a'.
quests.flowRule: Vowel-to-Vowel Glides: /aɪ/ followed by a vowel tends to get a /j/ bridge.

quests.instruction: Shadow the instruction. What links 'do it'?
quests.word: Do it again, but slower this time.
quests.textToSpeak: Do it again, but slower this time.
quests.ipa: /ˈduː‿ɪt əˈɡen | bət ˈsləʊə ðɪs ˈtaɪm/
quests.hint: Notice your lips rounding.
quests.explanation: /uː/ ends with rounded lips, so a /w/ glide bridges into the next vowel: doo-wit.
quests.flowRule: Vowel-to-Vowel Glides: /uː/ is followed by a /w/ bridge.

quests.instruction: Shadow the review. Which sound often appears between 'saw' and 'a' in many accents?
quests.word: I saw a film about it last night.
quests.textToSpeak: I saw a film about it last night.
options: A /j/ glide, because the vowel is a front vowel
A /w/ glide, because the lips round after /ɔː/
quests.ipa: /aɪ ˈsɔːr‿ə ˈfɪlm əˈbaʊt‿ɪt ˈlɑːst ˈnaɪt/
quests.hint: Think of how 'law and order' sounds.
quests.explanation: In non-rhotic accents, an /r/ can link /ɔː/ with a following vowel.
quests.flowRule: Intrusive /r/: an extra /r/ often bridges /ɔː/, /ɑː/ or /ə/ and a following vowel.

quests.instruction: Shadow the complaint. What happens at 'last night'?
quests.word: Last night we couldn't find a parking space.
quests.textToSpeak: Last night we couldn't find a parking space.
options: The /t/ of 'last' is often dropped between /s/ and /n/
quests.correctAnswer: The /t/ of 'last' is often dropped between /s/ and /n/
quests.ipa: /ˈlɑːs ˈnaɪt wi ˈkʊdnt ˈfaɪnd ə ˈpɑːkɪŋ ˈspeɪs/
quests.hint: Say 'last night' quickly and listen.
quests.explanation: Clusters like /st/ followed by a consonant simplify in relaxed speech, so 'last' loses its /t/.
quests.flowRule: Consonant Cluster Simplification: a middle /t/ or /d/ drops between two consonants.

quests.instruction: Shadow the urgent remark. What happens to 'have to'?
quests.word: We'll have to get a move on.
quests.textToSpeak: We'll have to get a move on.
quests.ipa: /wiːl ˈhæf tə ˈɡet‿ə ˈmuːv ˈɒn/
quests.hint: Compare how the final sound of 'have' behaves in 'have a look' versus 'have to go'.
quests.explanation: Before the voiceless /t/ of 'to', the voiced /v/ loses its voicing and becomes /f/, so 'have to' sounds like /hæftə/ even though it is spelled with a v.
quests.flowRule: Voicing Assimilation: /v/ weakens to /f/ before a voiceless /t/ in 'have to'.

quests.instruction: Shadow the reply. Which two words blend most smoothly in the first part?
quests.word: Give me a minute, I'm almost done.
quests.textToSpeak: Give me a minute, I'm almost done.
options: 'me a' — the /m/ is dropped between the two words
'give me' — the /v/ is weak and flows straight into the /m/
quests.correctAnswer: 'give me' — the /v/ is weak and flows straight into the /m/
quests.ipa: /ˈɡɪv mi ə ˈmɪnɪt | aɪm ˈɔːlməʊst ˈdʌn/
quests.hint: Notice how 'me' and 'a' connect.
quests.explanation: 'Me a' links with /m/ sliding onto /ə/, forming a quick unit.
quests.flowRule: Consonant-to-Vowel Linking: /m/ moves onto a following weak vowel.

quests.instruction: Shadow the compliment. What happens at 'best meal'?
quests.word: That was the best meal I've had in ages.
quests.textToSpeak: That was the best meal I've had in ages.
options: Both /t/ and /m/ are fully released with a pause
The /t/ of 'best' is often dropped or lightly held
'best' becomes 'bes' with extra stress on the /s/
quests.correctAnswer: The /t/ of 'best' is often dropped or lightly held
quests.ipa: /ðət wəz ðə ˈbest ˈmiːl aɪv ˈhæd‿ɪn ˈeɪdʒɪz/
quests.hint: Listen to the consonants in the middle.
quests.explanation: The /t/ is barely audible between /s/ and /m/, which makes 'best meal' flow.
quests.flowRule: Consonant Cluster Simplification: the /t/ in '-st' is weak before another consonant.

quests.instruction: Shadow the table request. What happens at 'pass me'?
quests.word: Can you pass me the salt and pepper?
quests.textToSpeak: Can you pass me the salt and pepper?
quests.ipa: /kən jʊ ˈpɑːs mi ðə ˈsɔːlt ən ˈpepə/
quests.hint: Say 'pass me' without a gap.
quests.explanation: The /s/ flows directly into /m/ with no gap between the words.
quests.flowRule: Smooth Transition: consonant-to-consonant boundaries are smoothly connected.

quests.instruction: Shadow the agreement. What happens at 'good idea'?
quests.word: I think that's a good idea, to be honest.
quests.textToSpeak: I think that's a good idea, to be honest.
options: The /d/ links onto 'idea', so it sounds like 'goo-didea'
A full pause after 'good' keeps the /d/ crisp
'good' becomes 'goo' with no final consonant at all
quests.correctAnswer: The /d/ links onto 'idea', so it sounds like 'goo-didea'
quests.ipa: /aɪ ˈθɪŋk ðæts ə ˈɡʊd aɪˈdɪə | tə bi ˈɒnɪst/
quests.hint: Think about how /d/ meets a vowel.
quests.explanation: 'Good' ends in /d/ and 'idea' starts with a vowel, so the /d/ slides onto the next word.
quests.flowRule: Consonant-to-Vowel Linking: /d/ links over word boundaries before a vowel.

quests.instruction: Shadow the news. What happens to 'friend from'?
quests.word: My friend from Madrid is visiting this weekend.
quests.textToSpeak: My friend from Madrid is visiting this weekend.
quests.ipa: /maɪ ˈfrend frəm məˈdrɪd ɪz ˈvɪzɪtɪŋ ðɪs ˌwiːkˈend/
quests.hint: Say 'friend from' quickly and feel the tongue.
quests.explanation: In fast speech the /d/ is often deleted before a consonant, so 'friend from' sounds like 'fren from'.
quests.flowRule: Elision: a final /d/ or /t/ can drop before another consonant.

quests.instruction: Shadow the request. What happens at 'hold the'?
quests.word: Hold the door, I'm right behind you.
quests.textToSpeak: Hold the door, I'm right behind you.
options: The /h/ of 'hold' vanishes, leaving 'old the door'
quests.ipa: /ˈhəʊld ðə ˈdɔː | aɪm ˈraɪt bɪˈhaɪnd jʊ/
quests.hint: Listen to the end of 'hold'.
quests.explanation: 'Hold the' has /d/ before /ð/, which makes the /d/ hard to hear.
quests.flowRule: Elision: a /d/ before /ð/ is weak or dropped.

quests.instruction: Shadow the instruction. What happens in 'asked me'?
quests.word: She asked me to wait by the entrance.
quests.textToSpeak: She asked me to wait by the entrance.
options: The /k/ is fully released, giving 'ask-t me' clearly
The /t/ is stressed and held longer than the /k/
quests.ipa: /ʃi ˈɑːskt mi tə ˈweɪt baɪ ði ˈentrəns/
quests.hint: Say 'asked me' quickly.
quests.explanation: Triple consonants simplify: /kt/ becomes a single stop before /m/.
quests.flowRule: Consonant Cluster Simplification: /kt/ clusters lose the middle sound.

quests.instruction: Shadow the apology. What happens at 'meant to'?
quests.word: I meant to tell you earlier, honestly.
quests.textToSpeak: I meant to tell you earlier, honestly.
quests.ipa: /aɪ ˈment tə ˈtel jʊ ˈɜːliə | ˈɒnɪstli/
quests.hint: Listen to the two /t/ sounds.
quests.explanation: Two /t/ sounds collide and merge into one longer /t/.
quests.flowRule: Same-Sound Merging: when identical sounds meet, they are pronounced as one.

quests.instruction: Shadow the offer. Where does /j/ merge?
quests.word: Would you like me to show you the way?
quests.textToSpeak: Would you like me to show you the way?
options: 'like me' — the /k/ and /m/ fuse into one sound
'the way' — the /ð/ changes to a /d/ before 'way'
quests.ipa: /wʊdʒə ˈlaɪk mi tə ˈʃəʊ juː ðə ˈweɪ/
quests.hint: Think of how /d/ + /j/ becomes /dʒ/.
quests.explanation: 'Would you' merges /d/ + /j/ to /dʒ/. 'Show you' keeps a /w/ glide instead.
quests.flowRule: Coalescence: /d/ + /j/ often merge into /dʒ/ in relaxed speech.

quests.instruction: Shadow the quick question. What happens at 'did you'?
quests.word: Did you eat yet, or should I order?
quests.textToSpeak: Did you eat yet, or should I order?
quests.ipa: /dɪdʒə ˈiːt ˈjet | ɔː ʃəd aɪ ˈɔːdə/
quests.hint: Say 'did you' as one word.
quests.explanation: /d/ and /j/ merge into /dʒ/ in relaxed speech.
quests.flowRule: Coalescence: /d/ + /j/ → /dʒ/ in 'did you' is extremely common.

quests.instruction: Shadow the confession. What happens to 'going to'?
quests.word: I'm not going to lie, that was tough.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm not going to lie, that was tough.
options: It's fully pronounced in a formal way
quests.ipa: /aɪm ˈnɒt ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə ˈlaɪ | ðət wəz ˈtʌf/
quests.hint: Say the phrase as a speaker who is about to confess something quickly.
quests.explanation: In relaxed speech, 'going to' before a verb shrinks to /ɡənə/, so 'I'm not gonna lie' becomes a quick lead-in before the real admission 'that was tough'.
quests.flowRule: Reduced Forms: 'going to' + verb compresses to 'gonna' in casual speech.

quests.instruction: Shadow the question. What does 'did you put the' sound like?
quests.word: Right, where did you put the receipt?
quests.textToSpeak: Right, where did you put the receipt?
options: Each word is separate and equal

quests.hint: Hear how 'did you' blends.
quests.explanation: The function words between 'where' and 'put' are compressed.
quests.flowRule: Weak Forms Plus Coalescence: 'did you' blends before the main verb.

quests.instruction: Shadow the estimate. What happens at 'might take'?
quests.word: It might take us a few days.
quests.textToSpeak: It might take us a few days.
options: The two /t/ sounds merge into one long /t/: 'migh-take'
quests.correctAnswer: The two /t/ sounds merge into one long /t/: 'migh-take'

quests.hint: Say 'might take' without stopping.
quests.explanation: Final /t/ of 'might' and initial /t/ of 'take' form one long /t/.
quests.flowRule: Same-Sound Merging: two /t/ sounds are pronounced as one long sound.

quests.instruction: Shadow the plan. What happens at 'let me'?
quests.word: Let me see if I can move this appointment.
quests.textToSpeak: Let me see if I can move this appointment.
options: 'let' is stressed and 'me' is whispered afterwards
'me' becomes a full /miː/ and takes the beat

quests.hint: Imagine a friend saying this while checking a calendar and typing at the same time.
quests.explanation: The /t/ of 'let' is absorbed by the following /m/, and 'me' weakens, so 'let me see' flows as 'lemme see' and the speaker's real focus lands on 'move' and 'appointment'.
quests.flowRule: Reduced Forms: 'let me' compresses into a single quick syllable group in casual speech.

quests.instruction: Shadow the praise. What happens to 'kind of'?
quests.word: She's the kind of person you can rely on.

'kind' is whispered so that 'of' can be heard

quests.hint: Listen to the end of 'kind'.
quests.explanation: 'Of' reduces to /ə/ and 'kind' links to it: /kaɪndə/.
quests.flowRule: Reduced Forms: 'kind of' links and reduces to /kaɪndə/.

quests.instruction: Shadow the suggestion. Which sound bridges 'go in'?

quests.textToSpeak: Shall we get a coffee before we go in?

quests.flowRule: Vowel-to-Vowel Glides: /w/ follows rounded vowels like /əʊ/.

quests.instruction: Shadow the reflection. What happens at 'believe how'?
quests.word: I can't believe how quickly it's gone.
quests.textToSpeak: I can't believe how quickly it's gone.

The /h/ is silent, so 'how' sounds like 'ow'

quests.hint: Hear the transition from 'believe' to 'how'.
quests.explanation: The /v/ is pronounced smoothly into the /h/; they blend without a break.
quests.flowRule: Smooth Transition: a voiced sound before /h/ flows into it.

quests.instruction: Shadow the question. What happens at 'have you'?
quests.word: Have you seen the photo she sent me?
quests.textToSpeak: Have you seen the photo she sent me?
options: 'have' is stressed as /hæv/ and 'you' is clearly /juː/
'you' is silent, so it sounds like 'have seen'

quests.explanation: 'Have' keeps its /v/ but 'you' weakens to /jə/, so the pair becomes a fast /hævjə/ that glides into the stressed 'seen'.
quests.flowRule: Weak Forms Plus Linking: 'you' reduces to /jə/ and attaches to the word before it.

quests.instruction: Shadow the frustration. What happens at 'drove all'?
quests.word: We drove all the way there, and it was closed.
quests.textToSpeak: We drove all the way there, and it was closed.

'all' is whispered while 'drove' gets a long pause

quests.explanation: The /v/ ends 'drove' and 'all' starts with a vowel, so the consonant slides across the boundary: 'dro-vall', which keeps the frustrated sentence flowing.
quests.flowRule: Consonant-to-Vowel Linking: a voiced consonant moves onto the next word's vowel without a break.

quests.instruction: Shadow the promise. Which chain is connected?

quests.explanation: 'As soon as I' has three consonant-to-vowel links in a row: a-soo-na-zai.
quests.flowRule: Consonant-to-Vowel Linking: repeated structures create long chains.

quests.instruction: Shadow the casual question. What happens at 'want to'?
quests.word: Do you want to grab something on the way?
quests.textToSpeak: Do you want to grab something on the way?

'to' becomes a full /tuː/ with its own beat

quests.instruction: Shadow the explanation. Which links recur in the second half?

quests.textToSpeak: It's not that I don't like it, I just can't afford it.

'just can't' — the /t/ is stressed and strongly released
'I just' — the /j/ is silent, so it sounds like 'I ust'
quests.correctAnswer: 'can't afford it' — a chain with /t/ and /d/ moving forward
quests.ipa: /ɪts ˈnɒt ðət aɪ ˈdəʊnt ˈlaɪk‿ɪt | aɪ ˈdʒʌst ˈkɑːnt‿əˈfɔːd‿ɪt/
quests.hint: Hear how the second half flows.
quests.explanation: 'Can't' ends in /t/ before 'afford'; 'afford' ends in /d/ before 'it', so both links continue.
quests.flowRule: Consonant-to-Vowel Linking: multiple short links can build a fast sentence-ending chain.

quests.instruction: Shadow the reassurance. Which sound connects 'over' and 'in'?
quests.word: She'll be over in a minute or two.
quests.textToSpeak: She'll be over in a minute or two.
quests.ipa: /ʃiːl bi ˈəʊvər‿ɪn‿ə ˈmɪnɪt‿ɔː ˈtuː/
quests.hint: Look at the last letter of 'over'.
quests.explanation: In non-rhotic accents the written 'r' is silent until a vowel follows, so it reappears: /əʊvər ɪn/.
quests.flowRule: Linking /r/: a final spelled 'r' is pronounced before a vowel-initial word.
